newsitem.title: USA: WMX Technologies mulling sale of interests - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: WMX Technologies mulling sale of interests - WSJ.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc is considering selling its interests in two companies in a move that could bring it $1 billion or more, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
But the newspaper said the company would not be able to sell its interest until 1998 due to agreements it had with both companies.
The sales would also have to be approved by the two companies, namely ServiceMaster and Wessex Water, it added.
Phillip Rooney, the company's chief executive officer, told the newspaper he had yet to decide "with certainty" whether to sell the companies.
Rooney said the company was also thinking about issuing convertible-debt securities that would give it the option to repay holders with shares of the two companies instead of cash.
WMX owns about 27.2 million shares or 18 percent of ServiceMaster, a commercial and residential cleaning and services concern.
It also holds about 20 percent or 50.7 million shares in Wessex, a water utility.

Rooney also told the newspaper that WMX would cut its capital spending for 1997 to under $1 billion from $1.1 billion this year. It is using its cash to buy back shares in WMX and a majority owned unit, Wheelabrator Technologies Inc, he said.
